newsitem.title: TURKEY: Iraqi oil minister in Turkey for gas sale talks.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi oil minister in Turkey for gas sale talks.

text.p: Iraqi Oil Minister Amir Muhammad Rasheed arrived in Turkey on Tuesday for a joint economic meeting and talks on possible Iraqi gas sales to Turkey, officials said.

"There is the right potential to develop the two countries' relations. A contribution can be made to the issue of natural gas and oil from Iraq," Anatolian news agency quoted Rasheed as telling a news conference at Ankara airport.
"There is also the possibility of fruitful cooperation in petrochemicals," he said.

Turkish officials said the two countries would take up bilateral trade, Iraq's purchases of food items from Turkey under the U.N. oil-for-food deal and possible Iraqi natural gas sales to Turkey through a pipeline to be built.
Iraq and Turkey may sign a contract for the gas deal, the details of which have not been given, they said.
Turkish and Iraqi officials said in the summer after a meeting in Baghdad that the designed capacity of the pipeline would be 10 billion cubic metres a year.

Rasheed is to participate on Wednesday in the first joint economic meeting with Turkey in the six years since the Gulf crisis. He will hold talks with State Minister Ahmet Cemil Tunc, who is in charge of affairs with Iraq.
Turkey's state oil refinery Tupras has begun buying 75,000 barrels per day (bpd) of Iraqi oil under the U.N. deal.
The sides are expected to discuss Turkey's sales of pulses and sugar to Iraq under the U.N. deal which allows Iraq to sell oil worth $2 billion over six months to buy food and medicine.

Iraqi oil flow through Turkey's southern Ceyhan oil terminal, which pumped out one third of Iraqi oil exports before the U.N. sanctions were slapped on Baghdad in 1990, resumed earlier this month after the United Nations agreed Iraq could begin limited oil sales.
Turkey offered to sell 50,000 tonnes of sugar to Iraq and international traders said Iraq could buy all of its planned pulses, hygenic material and edible oil purchases from Turkey.
Under the U.N. deal Iraq's pulses purchases are expected to be worth $102 million, hygenic material $65 million, sugar $115 million and edible oil $111 million.
Rasheed, who visited Turkey in March to inspect preparations for Ceyhan terminal for Iraq use under the U.N. plan, is expected to leave Turkey on Saturday.
